protocol.py: VERIFIED against plate map dil-03. 8 of 8 wells hold what the plate map says.
  Destination: NEST 96 Well Plate 200 µL Flat (slot 2). Reading of the request: 8 standards;
    excess removed from the last well.

Labware for the technique (Serial dilution): nothing to flag.

Where every liquid ended up (ul):
  liquid                             declared delivered in source elsewhere    lost
  bsa                                   200.0      99.6     100.0       0.4     0.0
  water                                6000.0     300.4    5699.6       0.0     0.0
  Note: bsa ends in wells the plate map does not list for it: B1 in slot 3 (0.4 ul).

Prep sheet: what to put on the deck before the run.
  slot labware                               well  liquid                       load at least  declared
  3    Opentrons 24 Tube Rack with NEST 1.5  A1    bsa                                  100.0     200.0
  3    Opentrons 24 Tube Rack with NEST 1.5  B1    water                                  0.0    1000.0  already in the plate: 1000 ul declared, nothing drawn
  4    NEST 12 Well Reservoir 15 mL          A1    water                                350.0    5000.0
  Tips: 16 from Opentrons OT-2 96 Tip Rack 300 µL in slot 1.
  'Load at least' is what the robot draws. Add the dead volume of your tube or reservoir.
  A well 'already in the plate' is declared to hold liquid before the run and the robot only
    adds to it: put in what is declared.

This checks the logic of the protocol: what goes where, and how much. It does not check the
  physics: whether a viscous liquid is pipetted accurately, or a drop stays on a tip.

check_text:
protocol.py: 4 biology problems (1 error, 2 warnings, 1 note).

1. ERROR PIPETTE-RANGE: 5 ul is below what the p300_single_gen2 can measure (20 ul at least)
   line 51:  p300.mix(10, 5, target_well)
   At line 51 the p300_single_gen2 is asked to draw 5 ul, below its minimum of 20 ul (this
   line did it 80 times). A pipette cannot measure less than its minimum: it draws the wrong
   amount, or nothing, and the volumes in this protocol only add up on paper. The simulator
   passes the move. Wells: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7 and A8 in slot 2.
   Affected: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7 and A8 in slot 2.
   Fix: Use a pipette whose range covers the volume (a p20 for 1 to 20 ul), or scale the
   reaction so every volume is at least the pipette's minimum.
   Source: Opentrons: pipette characteristics (volume ranges)
           https://docs.opentrons.com/v2/pipettes/characteristics.html
   Source: Integra: pipetting tips (work at 35 to 100% of nominal volume)
           https://www.integra-biosciences.com/united-states/en/pipetting-tips
   [a0754d435628]

2. WARNING MIX-TOO-WEAK: Mixing too weak to stir 7 wells: 10 × 5 ul in 100 ul
   line 51:  p300.mix(10, 5, target_well)
   At line 51 the tip mixes wells A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7 and A8 in slot 2 with 10 strokes of
   5 ul in a well holding 100 ul (this line did it 7 times). 10 strokes of 5 ul move 0.5 of
   the well in all; it takes about 2 wells' worth of strokes to mix (the mixing work).
   Integra draws over 80% of the well five times; three mixes gave 11.8% CV where twenty
   gave 1.7%. What the well holds is not at the concentration you calculated, and in a
   dilution series every later step inherits the error.
   Affected: wells A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7 and A8 in slot 2.
   Fix: Mix the well with about 80% of its volume (80 ul) at least 5 times: `mix(5, 80,
   well)`. A stroke of the whole well draws air; use no more than 90%.
   Source: Integra: how to perform serial dilutions
           https://www.integra-biosciences.com/global/en/applicationguide/master-art-pipetting-and-learn-how-perform-serial-dilutions-our-comprehensive-guide
   Source: Integra: three serial-dilution protocols (over 80% of the volume, five times)
           https://www.integra-biosciences.com/global/en/applications/3-simple-and-proven-automation-protocols-serial-dilutions-assist-plus-pipetting-robot
   Source: Beckman AMPure XP instructions (mix with a tip volume just below the well volume)
           https://research.fredhutch.org/content/dam/research/hahn/methods/Agencourt%20AMPure%20XP.pdf
   Source: Esca Automation: serial dilution, a classic technique
           https://escaautomation.substack.com/p/serial-dilution-a-classic-technique
   Source: labautomation.io 3654: how to mix a bacteria sample enough
           https://labautomation.io/t/how-to-mix-bacteria-sample-enough/3654
   Source: Artel: automated liquid handlers as sources of error
           https://www.bioprocessintl.com/assays/automated-liquid-handlers-as-sources-of-error
   [d861c6822f63]

3. WARNING UNMIXED-AT-END: Tube B1 in slot 3 never mixed after bsa went in (5% of the well)
   line 57:  p300.dispense(50, tuberack["B1"])
   At line 57 the robot added bsa to tube B1 in slot 3, which already held water. The
   addition was 5% of the well, nothing mixed the well afterwards, and the run ended with it
   that way. Two liquids layered in a small well do not mix on their own, so what the well
   holds is not at the concentration you calculated. The liquid added last is a sample, so
   nothing else in the workflow will mix it: a normalisation or a pool left like this is not
   what it says it is.
   Affected: tube B1 in slot 3.
   Fix: Mix tube B1 in slot 3 after line 57: `mix_after=(5, 840)` on the transfer, or
   `pipette.mix(5, 840, well)`, with the volume about 80% of what the well holds.
   Source: Artel: automated liquid handlers as sources of error
           https://www.bioprocessintl.com/assays/automated-liquid-handlers-as-sources-of-error
   Source: Illumina: normalising library concentrations (pipette up and down 10 times to
   mix)
           https://support.illumina.com/ko-kr/bulletins/2017/03/best-practices-for-manually-normalizing-library-concentrations.html
   Source: Thermo PowerTrack user guide (a reaction plate not mixed well gives variable
   replicates)
           https://documents.thermofisher.com/TFS-Assets/LSG/manuals/MAN0018825_PowerTrackSYBRGreenMasterMix_UG.pdf
   Source: Integra: how to perform serial dilutions
           https://www.integra-biosciences.com/global/en/applicationguide/master-art-pipetting-and-learn-how-perform-serial-dilutions-our-comprehensive-guide
   [25a35cd27696]

4. NOTE NO-NEGATIVE-CONTROL: No blank on a dilution series: 8 wells of bsa
   line 49:  p300.dispense(step["transfer_vol"], target_well)
   At line 49 the robot starts a dilution series of bsa in NEST 96 Well Plate 200 µL Flat
   (slot 2): 8 wells at 8 concentrations, each level about 2 times weaker than the one
   before. No well on this plate holds water with no sample, so there is no blank: the curve
   has no zero to read against, and a signal from the diluent or the plastic cannot be told
   from the lowest point. Wells: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7 and A8 in slot 2.
   Affected: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7 and A8 in slot 2.
   Fix: Add a well of water alone, and tell the plate map where it is.
   Source: MIQE 2009: a no-template control on every plate is essential
           https://gene-quantification.com/miqe-bustin-et-al-clin-chem-2009.pdf
   Source: MIQE 2.0 (2025): the no-template and no-RT controls, still essential
           https://academic.oup.com/clinchem/article/71/6/634/8119148
   Source: Bustin 2025: MIQE compliance remains patchy
           https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/PMC12154065/fullTextXML
   Source: Qiagen bench guide: PCR controls (no-template, no-RT, positive)
           https://www.qiagen.com/en-us/knowledge-and-support/knowledge-hub/bench-guide/pcr/reference-genes-and-controls/pcr-controls
   Source: Bio-Rad real-time PCR applications guide: controls in triplicate
           https://www.bio-rad.com/webroot/web/pdf/lsr/literature/Bulletin_5279.pdf
   Source: Thermo Maxima SYBR manual: the NTC contains all components except template DNA
           https://assets.fishersci.com/TFS-Assets/LSG/manuals/MAN0012933_Maxima_SYBR_Green_qPCR_Master_ROX_Sol__k0251_UG.pdf
   [90b97d2495d5]

The Opentrons simulator (8.8.2) passed this protocol with no error: it checks that the robot
can make the moves, not what they do to the liquids.
